articles.title: Indian navy rescues 20 crew from Iranian fishing boat hijacked off Somalia
articles.summary: Indian naval forces successfully rescued an Iranian fishing vessel and its 20-member crew, which had been hijacked off the coast of Somalia. The complex anti-piracy operation, confirmed by India's Defense Ministry, lasted over 48 hours. This swift action highlights the Indian Navy's robust capability and commitment to ensuring maritime security and freedom of navigation in critical international shipping lanes.

articles.title: Saudi Pro League postpones matches after Asian Cup rescheduling
articles.summary: Saudi Arabia's premier football league (SPL) has postponed upcoming matches following the rescheduling of the AFC Asian Cup 2027. This decision impacts the domestic football calendar, highlighting the ripple effects of major international sporting event changes. Aspirants should note how such logistical adjustments are managed, demonstrating planning and adaptability in diverse fields.

articles.title: Dronemaker Stark Designs Uncrewed Ship to Hunt Russia’s Shadow Fleet
articles.summary: German startup Stark Defence plans to launch a 24-meter uncrewed surface vessel (USV) next year, signaling a major expansion beyond its small drone operations. This development highlights the increasing focus on autonomous naval technology. For SSB aspirants, this exemplifies advancements in unmanned systems, which are crucial for future maritime defence, surveillance, and patrol, showcasing evolving military capabilities and technological integration.

articles.title: Why have the Yankees kept all their coaches?
articles.summary: Matt Blake, consistently considered one of baseball's best pitching coaches, became the Yankees' highest-profile free agent this year. His tenure since 2020 has been instrumental in player development. His potential departure is a significant event for the team, underscoring the crucial role of coaching staff in professional sports performance and team strategy.

articles.title: Dhinidhi Desinghu's Bronze: A New Dawn For Indian Swimming
articles.summary: Sixteen-year-old Dhinidhi Desinghu has achieved a historic feat for India, securing the nation's first-ever swimming medal at the Youth Olympics held in Dakar. This remarkable accomplishment by the young athlete marks a significant milestone for Indian aquatic sports, inspiring future generations and highlighting India's growing presence on the global sporting stage.

articles.title: Chinese, Russian defence officials hail military ties
articles.summary: Russia's Defence Minister Andrei Belousov visited Beijing to strengthen military ties, with both nations hailing their 'stronger-than-ever' relations. This high-level engagement signifies a deepening strategic alignment and military cooperation between Moscow and Beijing, crucial for understanding evolving global power dynamics and regional security implications, especially for an SSB aspirant observing international defence postures.

articles.title: 13 Things I Found on the Internet Today (Vol.782)
articles.summary: Dufayel, established in 1856 as Palais de la Nouveauté, evolved into one of the globe's foremost department stores. It gained fame for its innovative model of selling furniture and household goods extensively on credit, achieving considerable business prominence during its peak.

articles.title: Why injuries to Thunder's Williams, Wallace could take so long to heal
articles.summary: During a recent game, Thunder team players Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace both sustained serious injuries. Williams suffered a gruesome ankle injury, while Wallace was diagnosed with a torn labrum in his shoulder. Reports indicate Williams has already begun treatment. These simultaneous setbacks present a considerable challenge for the team's upcoming performance and player roster management.

articles.title: 'I Didn't Want To Make A Film About A Remote India'
articles.summary: The creator of 'Pyre' outlines it as a brief story about two characters. Through their lives, the work aims to explore major societal themes impacting a changing India, including migration, ageing challenges, loneliness, and the quest for belonging. It promises a nuanced commentary on the nation's evolving social fabric and cultural dynamics.

articles.summary: Former Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh has urged Defence Minister Rajnath Singh to retain the 'Race Course' land under the Indian Air Force's operational control. This significant appeal underscores the strategic importance of defence land management and infrastructure for national security.
